description: A.J.A & FRIENDS - will we tell the best story?
summary:
NSOROMA ARCHIVES is an inclusive digital space museum that turns NASA’s scattered hardware records into stories anyone can explore. Thousands of machines have been sent into space, yet their histories sit in technical documents that are hard to read and rarely designed for people who are blind, have low vision, or are deaf or hard of hearing.

We built a responsive website where each machine has its own page with a plain-language explanation, mission facts, a written description of how it looks, a read-aloud description, an interactive 3D model and, where available, a captioned video with a transcript and sign-language interpretation. Visitors can search and filter the archive, choose standard, audio-first or visual-first exploration, and change text size, contrast and motion at any time. Mission status is always shown with a word, a shape and a colour.

It addresses the challenge by making NASA’s hardware history understandable and reachable for everyone. Our idea is simple: space exploration should not be limited by how someone experiences the world.
details:
What it does: NSOROMA ARCHIVES is a responsive museum site covering seven NASA machines so far: the Apollo 11 Lunar Module, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Ingenuity, Pioneer 10 and Pioneer 11. Visitors search and filter by environment, category, era and status, then open a full page for each machine with a plain-language story, mission facts, sources, a 3D model, audio and video.

Accessibility: we built toward WCAG 2.2 AA with semantic structure, full keyboard use, visible focus, screen-reader labels, text-size, high-contrast and reduced-motion controls, read-aloud descriptions, captions, transcripts and a written description of every 3D model. An optional welcome screen offers standard, audio-first or visual-first exploration without asking anyone to identify as disabled.

How it works: all machine data lives in one JSON file, and a check blocks publishing any video without captions and a transcript. Facts come from NASA’s NSSDCA and NASA Science mission pages; every record lists its sources and is flagged until verified.

Tools: React, Vite, Google model-viewer, the Web Speech API, Vercel and GitHub, with Syne and Questrial fonts. Parts of the code and text were written with the AI assistant Claude, as acknowledged on the site.
